decisions.reason: Uses the install log and manifest to show that fs-ext@2.1.1, pulled in by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, fails in its node-gyp configure build script because no Visual Studio/MSVC is present.
Cites the top-level flock import in lease.ts. Explains that --ignore-scripts leaves no native binary, so the import throws at load time on Windows before any branch runs, and the service cannot boot.

Distinguishes the Windows path (acquireLockHandleWin32 using a named kernel semaphore) from the POSIX flock path. Concludes a win32-only import-safe stub is safe because Windows keeps its semaphore and POSIX keeps real flock.

Follows the node-pty precedent with pnpm patch. Guards the install script to skip node-gyp on win32 and gives the entry a win32 pure-JS flock fallback with a compatible callback shape, keeping native on other platforms. Registers the patch under patchedDependencies with allowBuilds, and proposes reinstall, module-load and boot checks.
Explicitly respects the no-Visual-Studio constraint and treats the local pnpm patch as a repository overlay, leaving upstream sources and the pin untouched.
Cites DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 in full and ties it to the fs-ext install failure and the Windows patch recipe.

caps.reason: Installing Visual Studio is explicitly rejected.
--ignore-scripts is rejected, and the plan makes the entry loadable with a fallback.
The plan uses the local patchedDependencies mechanism and requires no upstream edit.
The no-op stub applies to win32 only. The Windows semaphore and POSIX flock are both preserved.
